item.title: Reverse a Short Function to C
item.description: Target: Windows x86-64 (fastcall: first two int args in ecx, edx; return in eax). Reverse this disassembly to equivalent C: foo: cmp ecx, edx / cmovle ecx, edx / mov eax, ecx / ret -- What does foo(int a, int b) compute? --- Answer: int foo(int a, int b) { if (a <= b) { a = b; } return a; } Equivalently: return (a > b) ? a : b; -- this is max(a, b). Explanation: 1) cmp ecx, edx sets flags for ecx - edx (a - b) without altering either register. 2) cmovle ecx, edx is a conditional move: it copies edx into ecx only if the previous compare's flags indicate a <= b, replacing a branch with data flow -- no jump is taken either way. 3) mov eax, ecx places the (possibly updated) ecx into the return register, so the function returns whichever of a/b is larger.
